reference_notes: The energy model (HOT2000) measures the thermal envelope, often for one unit of a multi-unit block, so its wall area is not compared; its ceiling area stands in for the footprint and its window area for the windows.
15 IFC models tag the whole 454 mm slab build-up as concrete where the drawings state 100-130 mm; those slabs are left out of the slab comparison.

The IFC model is not ground truth either: on AB_Fourplex_01 it omits the 76 mm below-grade rigid insulation that the drawings' F1 slab assembly calls for, so a rigid-insulation 'over-count' there is the model's gap, not ours.
Material gaps the tool already reports as not counted: floor joists and roof trusses (wood framing), foundation walls (concrete), steel studs, and the cladding and roofing placeholders.

carbon_vs_ifc_same_factors.note: Our carbon over the architect's IFC quantities priced with OUR factors, for the materials both name (concrete, gypsum, insulation, sheathing; framing excluded because the IFC models it as solid layers). This isolates quantity error from factor and module differences.

intensity_vs_cmhc_a1_a5.note: Our kg CO2e per m2 of measured floor area over CMHC's A1-A5 per m2 of its own floor area: robust to a report that covers one unit of a block the drawings show whole.

carbon_vs_cmhc_a1_a5.note: Our A1-A3 total over CMHC's reported A1-A5 for the same design. Below 1 is expected (A4 transport and A5 construction are not counted) and the rest of the gap is scope we flag as not counted: cladding and roofing placeholders, joists, trusses, steel studs, foundation walls.
